created notify: true alerts_added notify: true while firing; false while acknowledged or snoozed alert_replaced, alert_resolved, alert_continued, annotations_changed, severity_raised notify: false urgency_raised notify: true when the rise ends a Snooze or removes the acknowledgement; false otherwise reopened notify: true while firing or acknowledged; false while snoozed snooze_ended notify: true resolved notify: false moved_to_default_route notify: false acknowledged notify: false takeover notify: true unacknowledged notify: true when disabling or deleting the Owner released it; false for the Command unresolved, snoozed, unsnoozed, note_added notify: false ack_timeout notify: true unclaimed notify: false reminder notify: true reminder_answered notify: false auto_unacknowledged notify: true notices_missed notify: true

The event test is sent only by a Destination test: it carries test: true and sequence 0 and belongs to no Alert Group's order.

items.title: Versioning
items.text: New event names and new fields are added within version 1. Removing a field or changing its meaning needs a new version. Ignore event names and fields you do not know.

items.title: Order and duplicates
items.text:
• The events of one Alert Group are sent in order: the next one waits until the previous one is delivered or ends as Not delivered. Events of different Alert Groups do not wait for each other.
  • Delivery is at least once and never collapsed: a retry sends the same event again with the same webhook-id and the same body. Drop duplicates by webhook-id.
  • Events are never subject to Storms: during a Storm every event is sent, created of every Alert Group included.
  • While the Destination is Broken its events wait; after it recovers, every event that came due meanwhile is sent in order per Alert Group, none dropped and with no age limit.

items.title: How the answer counts
items.text:
2xx Delivered. 429 or 503 with Retry-After The same event is sent again exactly when asked. 408, any other 5xx, a timeout or a network error Retried with backoff; after delivery.transient_budget the Destination becomes Broken. 401, 403, 404, 410 The Destination becomes Broken; the event waits and is the probe. 400, 413, 422, a redirect, any other answer That event ends as Not delivered and the next one follows; the Destination stays healthy. A redirect is never followed; the error names its target.

Requests go through the outbound address policy: a URL that resolves to a link-local, cloud metadata, multicast or unspecified address is refused under every policy, and loopback and private addresses need an allowed network. A refused request makes the Destination Broken with the rule as the reason, because every later request would be refused too. A Broken outgoing webhook is probed with its oldest waiting event; with none waiting, the next event is attempted as soon as it comes due.

items.title: Verify the signature
items.text:
Every request carries three headers, in the style of the Standard Webhooks specification:

  • webhook-id — the id of the event, kept across retries;
  • webhook-timestamp — Unix seconds when the request was signed;
  • webhook-signature — one or more signatures v1,<base64>, separated by a space.

Each signature is the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of {webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body} — the raw body, byte for byte — with the key that is the base64 after whsec_ in the Signing secret. Accept a request when one of its signatures matches, compare in constant time, and refuse a timestamp more than five minutes from your clock.

Go:

func verify(secret, id, timestamp string, body []byte, header string) bool {
    key, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(strings.TrimPrefix(secret, "whsec_"))
    if err != nil {
        return false
    }
    ts, err := strconv.ParseInt(timestamp, 10, 64)
    if err != nil || math.Abs(time.Since(time.Unix(ts, 0)).Seconds()) > 300 {
        return false
    }
    mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
    mac.Write([]byte(id + "." + timestamp + "."))
    mac.Write(body)
    want := []byte(base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil)))
    for _, sig := range strings.Fields(header) {
        if v, s, ok := strings.Cut(sig, ","); ok && v == "v1" && hmac.Equal([]byte(s), want) {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}

Python:

import base64, hashlib, hmac, time

def verify(secret: str, msg_id: str, timestamp: str, body: bytes, header: str) -> bool:
    key = base64.b64decode(secret.removeprefix("whsec_"))
    try:
        if abs(time.time() - int(timestamp)) > 300:
            return False
    except ValueError:
        return False
    mac = hmac.new(key, f"{msg_id}.{timestamp}.".encode() + body, hashlib.sha256)
    want = base64.b64encode(mac.digest()).decode()
    for sig in header.split():
        version, _, value = sig.partition(",")
        if version == "v1" and hmac.compare_digest(value, want):
            return True
    return False

A shell, with openssl, to check a recorded request by hand — it compares neither in constant time nor the timestamp, so do not use it in a receiver — for a body saved in body.json:

KEY=$(printf '%s' "${SECRET#whsec_}" | base64 -d | od -An -v -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
EXPECTED="v1,$( { printf '%s.%s.' "$WEBHOOK_ID" "$WEBHOOK_TIMESTAMP"; cat body.json; } |
  openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC -macopt "hexkey:$KEY" -binary | base64)"
case " $WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE " in *" $EXPECTED "*) echo valid ;; *) echo invalid ;; esac

items.title: Regenerate and retire the Signing secret
items.text:
1. On the page of the Destination, under Signing secret, select Regenerate, and Regenerate again in the dialog. Muster shows the new secret once: deploy it to the receiving endpoint.

  2. Until you retire it, the previous secret still signs, and the Destination says since when. Once the endpoint verifies with the new secret, select Retire previous secret.

Through the API, POST /api/v1/destinations/{id}/signing-secret makes a new Signing secret and shows it once. Until you retire the previous one, requests carry two signatures — with the new and with the previous secret — and the Destination shows the warning previous_signing_secret_active with the date since when: deploy the new secret to the receiving endpoint, then retire the previous one with DELETE /api/v1/destinations/{id}/signing-secret/previous. Requests then carry one signature. Both changes are recorded in the Audit log, never with the secret. Rotating the master keys re-encrypts the Signing secrets but never changes them.

items.title: Delete the Destination
items.text: Deleting an events-mode Destination sends nothing more: its waiting events end as Not delivered with "the Destination was deleted", no final event is sent, and its secrets — the Signing secrets, the Secrets and the proxy password — are wiped at once, or as soon as a request that was already being sent ends.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
Four ways to use an outgoing webhook, built only from what it has: the events mode sends one signed event per lifecycle event; the template mode sends the requests you write and keeps their answers. Each recipe says which mode it uses and why.

These are sketches

The recipes show the shape of a setup, not a tested integration. The endpoints, fields and header names of the other system are examples, taken from the public documentation of an open tool. They change between versions and settings, so check them against the documentation of the version you run, and use Preview and Send test message on the Destination before you rely on it. In template mode, Send test message makes a real create request: on a status page or in an issue tracker it opens a real incident or issue, so send the first ones to a status page nobody reads or to a test repository. Everything about Muster in them is real: the modes, the fields the templates read, the extraction rules, the Secrets and the signature.

Common to all four:

  • Use a Route of its own. Create a Route whose Matchers pick only the Alerts you want to reach this system, for example severity="critical", and give it the webhook as its Destination. The other Routes are unaffected. See Routes and Group keys.
  • Keep credentials in Secrets, never in the URL or in a header as text. See Secrets.
  • Template mode follows Storms. While a Storm lasts, a template-mode Destination gets one Storm summary through its create request, and templates that read .AlertGroup fail for it. On a dedicated, narrow Route this rarely matters; otherwise branch on .Storm as Recipe: Storm summaries shows.
  • Look at the Request log when something does not work: it shows the requests Muster sent and the answers, with secrets masked. See Request log.

In the examples, MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL is https://muster.example.org.

items.title: A phone call or an SMS
items.text:
Mode: events. A provider with an HTTP API starts a call or sends a text when you post a small request to it. You want that only for the changes that need a human, and you want to send it once. The events mode fits, because every event carries notify, which is true exactly when the change is Loud, and a webhook-id that stays the same across retries.

Template mode does not fit here. It always has an update request, which sends again whenever its rendered update changes, and a call provider has nothing to update. It cannot decide to skip an event either.

Muster cannot know your provider's request, so put a small relay between them. The relay checks the signature, drops duplicates, picks the events worth a call, and calls the provider.

  1. Create a Destination of type webhook, mode events, with the relay's URL, as in Create the Destination. The relay below checks only the signature, so it needs the Secret token and its header from that example only when something in front of it asks for a credential. Keep the Signing secret that the answer shows once, and give it to the relay.
  2. Create a Route that matches what should ring a phone, with the Destination, and an On-call profile.
  3. Run the relay. This sketch is Python; the verify function is the one on Verify the signature:
import json, os, urllib.request
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

CALL_ON = {"created", "ack_timeout", "reopened"}   # the events worth a call
seen = set()                                        # webhook-ids; use a store with an expiry in real life

class Relay(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
        if not verify(os.environ["SIGNING_SECRET"], self.headers["webhook-id"],
                      self.headers["webhook-timestamp"], body, self.headers["webhook-signature"]):
            self.send_response(401); self.end_headers(); return
        event = json.loads(body)
        wid = self.headers["webhook-id"]
        if wid not in seen and event["notify"] and event["event"] in CALL_ON:
            group = event["alert_group"]
            call = urllib.request.Request(
                os.environ["PROVIDER_URL"],          # your provider's HTTP API
                json.dumps({"to": os.environ["ON_CALL_NUMBER"],
                            "text": f"Muster #{group['number']}: {group['title']}"}).encode(),
                {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["PROVIDER_TOKEN"],
                 "Content-Type": "application/json"})
            urllib.request.urlopen(call, timeout=10)  # an error here fails the request, and Muster retries the same event
            seen.add(wid)
        self.send_response(204); self.end_headers()

HTTPServer(("", 8080), Relay).serve_forever()

What to know:

  • Which events. created is a new Alert Group, ack_timeout a notice that nobody took it, and reopened a problem that returned. Leave out alerts_added and reminder, which are Loud too but only worth a message. The relay can also skip an Alert Group that is already acknowledged: every event carries the Alert Group's status as it was when the event was recorded.
  • Answer honestly. 2xx marks the event delivered. A 5xx makes Muster send the same event again with the same webhook-id. A 400 or 422 drops that one event. 401, 403, 404 and 410 make the Destination Broken, which is right for a relay that is misconfigured. See How the answer counts.
  • Test it. Send test message sends the event test with notify false. For the first run, add "test" to CALL_ON and replace event["notify"] in the condition with (event["notify"] or event["event"] == "test"), then change both back.

items.title: A status page
items.text:
Mode: template. A status page that has an HTTP API takes one incident per problem and lets you update it. That is the shape of the template mode: create opens the incident and extracts its id from the answer, and update changes it to the current state.

This sketch uses the incident API of the open status page Cachet 2.x as the example: a POST to /api/v1/incidents answers {"data": {"id": 7, …}}, and a PUT to /api/v1/incidents/7 changes it. Its status is 1 for investigating, 2 for identified and 4 for fixed. Create a Secret token with the page's API token.

create:

POST https://status.example.org/api/v1/incidents
X-Cachet-Token: {{ .Secrets.token }}
Content-Type: application/json

{"name": {{ .AlertGroup.Title | toJson }},
 "message": {{ .AlertGroup.Summary | toJson }},
 "status": 1,
 "visible": 1}

Extraction rule: the name id, the path $.data.id.

update:

PUT https://status.example.org/api/v1/incidents/{{ .Response.id }}
X-Cachet-Token: {{ .Secrets.token }}
Content-Type: application/json

{"name": {{ .AlertGroup.Title | toJson }},
 "message": {{ .AlertGroup.Summary | toJson }},
 "status": {{ if eq .AlertGroup.Status "resolved" }}4{{ else if eq .AlertGroup.Status "firing" }}1{{ else }}2{{ end }},
 "visible": 1}

The incident opens as investigating when an Alert Group appears, becomes identified while somebody has it or it is snoozed, and becomes fixed when the Alert Group resolves. If the Alert Group reopens, the next update says investigating again.

Think before you publish: the title and summary of an Alert Group come from your alert rules and may show internal names. Use a Route with Matchers for the alerts that are meant for your users, and write the summary annotations for them.

items.title: A second chat
items.text:
Mode: template. A chat with an open REST API and incoming messages is a Destination of its own: the same Alert Groups, in a second place. The template mode keeps one message per Alert Group in it, edits it where the chat's API allows, and posts the replies of the Thread.

This sketch uses the REST API of Rocket.Chat as the example. A POST to chat.postMessage answers with the message under message, with its _id and its room id rid; chat.update edits it; a message with a tmid is a reply in its thread. Create the Secrets token and user_id for the bot user's token and id.

create:

POST https://chat.example.org/api/v1/chat.postMessage
X-Auth-Token: {{ .Secrets.token }}
X-User-Id: {{ .Secrets.user_id }}
Content-Type: application/json

{"channel": "#alerts",
 "text": {{ printf "#%d %s (%s)\n%s" .AlertGroup.Number .AlertGroup.Title .AlertGroup.Status .AlertGroup.URL | toJson }}}

Extraction rules: id with $.message._id, and room with $.message.rid.

update:

POST https://chat.example.org/api/v1/chat.update
X-Auth-Token: {{ .Secrets.token }}
X-User-Id: {{ .Secrets.user_id }}
Content-Type: application/json

{"roomId": {{ .Response.room | toJson }},
 "msgId": {{ .Response.id | toJson }},
 "text": {{ printf "#%d %s (%s)\n%s" .AlertGroup.Number .AlertGroup.Title .AlertGroup.Status .AlertGroup.URL | toJson }}}

reply_in_thread:

POST https://chat.example.org/api/v1/chat.postMessage
X-Auth-Token: {{ .Secrets.token }}
X-User-Id: {{ .Secrets.user_id }}
Content-Type: application/json

{"roomId": {{ .Response.room | toJson }},
 "tmid": {{ .Response.id | toJson }},
 "text": {{ printf "%s on #%d" .Event .AlertGroup.Number | toJson }}}

What to know:

  • Edits may be limited by the chat. Many chats let a user edit a message only for a while, or not at all. If yours does, the update of an old message is refused, and by the chat's answer that ends as Not delivered or makes the Destination Broken. Check the chat's setting for editing messages. If you cannot allow edits, make update a second chat.postMessage call: each change is then a new message instead of an edit.
  • Loud and Quiet. A chat decides for itself what rings. Muster tells the template through .Notify, and through .Mentions whom to mention; wrap them in the chat's syntax with the mention function, as Mentions shows.
  • Two-step threads. A chat that needs a thread created first uses open_thread; see Recipe: a chat with two-step threads.

items.title: An issue tracker
items.text:
Mode: template. Opening an issue when a problem starts, commenting on it as it develops, and closing it when the problem resolves needs one thing: the id of the issue that the first request created, in every later request. That is what the extraction rules are for. The create request opens the issue and extracts its number, update changes its state, and reply_in_thread adds comments.

This sketch uses the issue API of the open forges Gitea and Forgejo, which share it. A POST to /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues answers with the issue, including its number; a PATCH to /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number} changes its state to open or closed; a POST to /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments adds a comment. Create a Secret token with an access token of a bot user that may write issues in the repository.

create:

POST https://git.example.org/api/v1/repos/ops/alerts/issues
Authorization: token {{ .Secrets.token }}
Content-Type: application/json

{"title": {{ printf "#%d %s" .AlertGroup.Number .AlertGroup.Title | toJson }},
 "body": {{ printf "%s\n\n%s" .AlertGroup.Summary .AlertGroup.URL | toJson }}}

Extraction rule: the name number, the path $.number.

update:

PATCH https://git.example.org/api/v1/repos/ops/alerts/issues/{{ .Response.number }}
Authorization: token {{ .Secrets.token }}
Content-Type: application/json

{"title": {{ printf "#%d %s (%s)" .AlertGroup.Number .AlertGroup.Title .AlertGroup.Status | toJson }},
 "state": "{{ if eq .AlertGroup.Status "resolved" }}closed{{ else }}open{{ end }}"}

reply_in_thread:

POST https://git.example.org/api/v1/repos/ops/alerts/issues/{{ .Response.number }}/comments
Authorization: token {{ .Secrets.token }}
Content-Type: application/json

{"body": {{ printf "%s: %s" .Event .AlertGroup.URL | toJson }}}

The issue opens with the Alert Group, gets a comment for each Thread reply, such as new Alerts, a Takeover or a Reminder, closes when the Alert Group is resolved, and opens again if the Alert Group returns. The title shows the current status.

What to know:

  • One issue per Alert Group. A Route that takes many Alert Groups opens many issues. Narrow its Matchers, or choose a Group key that groups more.
  • If the extraction finds nothing, the create still counts as delivered, the Timeline records the missing value, and every later request that reads it fails as a template error. Check the answer in the Send test message result, sent to a test repository.
  • A tracker whose answer carries no id cannot be driven this way. Use the events mode with a relay that remembers the id of the issue for each alert_group.id, and does what the recipe above does with the events created, resolved and reopened.

items.title: Outgoing webhook: template mode
items.text:
An outgoing webhook Destination in the template mode keeps one message per Alert Group in any chat that has a REST API, the way Muster keeps a message in Mattermost or Telegram: a create request posts it, an update request edits it to the current state, and optional open thread and reply in thread requests carry the follow-ups. You write each request as Go templates; Muster sends them, signed, and reads the values it needs from the answers.

The messages that Muster keeps in a messenger are customised with templates written the same way: see Messages and templates.

For an ordered stream of every lifecycle event instead, use the events mode; the mode both sends both.

In the examples, MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL is https://muster.example.org and the chat's API is https://chat.example.org/api.

items.title: Create the Destination
items.text:
In the web UI:

  1. Open Destinations, select Create destination, choose Outgoing webhook and the Mode Template (or Both, with the Events request too). Under Requests, Create and Update are required; Open thread and Reply in thread are optional.

  2. In Create, choose the Method, enter the URL, the headers with Add header and the Body, and add the extraction rules with Add rule: a name and a JSONPath into the answer.

  3. In Update, enter the request that edits the message; it reads the extracted values as {{ .Response.<name> }}.

  4. Give the Destination a Name and select Save. Muster shows the Signing secret once, as in the events mode, and then the saved Destination. In the screenshots, the chat's API is at https://hooks.example.org/chat/ops.

Through the API, create a Destination of type webhook with the mode template (or both, with the events request too):

{
  "type": "webhook",
  "name": "team chat",
  "mode": "template",
  "template": {
    "create": {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "https://chat.example.org/api/channels/ops/messages",
      "headers": [{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Bearer {{ .Secrets.token }}" }],
      "body": "{\"text\":{{ printf \"#%d %s (%s)\" .AlertGroup.Number .AlertGroup.Title .AlertGroup.Status | toJson }}}",
      "extract": [{ "name": "id", "path": "$.data.id" }]
    },
    "update": {
      "method": "PUT",
      "url": "https://chat.example.org/api/channels/ops/messages/{{ .Response.id }}",
      "headers": [{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Bearer {{ .Secrets.token }}" }],
      "body": "{\"text\":{{ printf \"#%d %s (%s)\" .AlertGroup.Number .AlertGroup.Title .AlertGroup.Status | toJson }}}"
    }
  },
  "proxy": { "enabled": false },
  "mentions": { "...": "Mention settings, as for any Destination" },
  "limiter": { "limit": 5, "per_seconds": 1 }
}

Each request has:

  • a method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE;
  • a URL, headers and an optional body, each a Go template in the same sandbox as message templates;
  • for create and open_thread only, extraction rules: a name and a JSONPath (RFC 9535) into the JSON answer.

create and update are required; open_thread and reply_in_thread are optional. When you save, every template is parsed and run on a dry run with a built-in example Alert Group, its Secrets and the values it may read filled with example-<name>; an error answers 422 at /template/<request>/<field> with its line and column. The URL must then be an absolute http or https URL.

Muster sets webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature on every request, signed with the Destination's Signing secret as in the events mode, Content-Type: application/json when a request has a body and no Content-Type header of its own, and User-Agent: Muster/<version> when it has no User-Agent of its own. The requests go through Muster's outbound address policy and the Destination's proxy; redirects are never followed. The answers map to outcomes as in the events mode.

items.title: What the templates read
items.text:
.AlertGroup Number, Title, Summary, Status, Route, SeverityLevel, Urgent, StartedAt, URL, ReopenCount, Owner; absent (nil) for a Storm summary. .Alerts The Alerts, as in Alertmanager: Status, Labels, Annotations, StartsAt, EndsAt, GeneratorURL, Fingerprint; with .Alerts.Firing and .Alerts.Resolved. .Status, .GroupLabels, .CommonLabels, .CommonAnnotations, .ExternalURL As in Alertmanager templates. .Storm For a Storm summary only: Route, AlertGroupCount, UrgentCount, Final (the Storm ended) and URL (the Route's Alert Groups in Muster). .Response The values the extraction rules found, by name. .Event The lifecycle event a Thread reply carries, such as alerts_added; empty otherwise. .Notify true when the message is Loud. .Mentions The Mention targets of a Loud message (see below). .Secrets The Destination's Secrets, by name. .Final In the final edit only: "No longer updated here; current state in Muster: {link}".

Alert data reach the templates as received, not escaped for any markup, because Muster does not know the chat's format. Write JSON bodies with toJson (or js inside a string), so that a label with a quote or a line break cannot break the body. A label or annotation the Alerts do not have is empty text, as in Alertmanager, so toJson gives "", not null; tell a missing value apart with if or or, as in {{ or .CommonLabels.team "none" }}.

Read a Secret as {{ .Secrets.<name> }} and an extracted value as {{ .Response.<name> }} — or with $. in front, or as {{ index .Secrets "<name>" }} with a quoted name. Any other use, such as {{ with .Secrets }}, {{ $s := .Secrets }} or {{ toJson .Response }}, is refused when you save: Muster checks before each request that every Secret and value a template reads exists, which it can only do for names written out. Printed or encoded whole, as {{ toJson . }} would, the Secrets show as [redacted].

items.title: Extraction rules and .Response
items.text:
A rule picks the first node its JSONPath selects in the JSON answer of create or open_thread — a string, a number as written, or a boolean — and stores it as a string under its name, per Alert Group and Destination. The first rule of create is also the message id Muster shows. create reads no values (it runs first), open_thread and update read those of create (an update can come before any thread exists), and reply_in_thread reads those of both.

When a rule finds nothing — the answer is not JSON, the path selects nothing, null, an object or an array, or a value longer than 1024 bytes — the create still counts as delivered, the Alert Group's Timeline records template_value_missing with the rule's name, and every later request that reads the value fails as a template error.

items.title: Reconciliation
items.text:
The template mode follows the Desired state like a messenger. The Desired state is the rendered update request (with Secrets and extracted values left out): when a change leaves it as it was, no request is made, and changes made while a request is pending collapse into the next update. Lifecycle events whose form is a Thread reply in the lifecycle event tables — new Alerts, a Takeover, a Reopen, an ack timeout notice, a Reminder… — go through reply_in_thread, batched like Thread replies in a messenger; without reply_in_thread they are not sent.

After the Destination was Broken, the template mode sends only the current state: one update per published Alert Group, no reply for the events of the period, and no create for an Alert Group that started and resolved meanwhile.

Deleting the Destination sends the final edit through update, with .Final set, and wipes its secrets once the final edits are done; in the mode both, the queued events end as Not delivered at once.

items.title: Recipe: a chat with one-step threads
items.text:
A reply is posted under the message:

"reply_in_thread": {
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "https://chat.example.org/api/channels/ops/messages/{{ .Response.id }}/replies",
  "headers": [{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Bearer {{ .Secrets.token }}" }],
  "body": "{\"text\":{{ printf \"%s on #%d\" .Event .AlertGroup.Number | toJson }},\"notify\":{{ .Notify }}}"
}

items.title: Recipe: a chat with two-step threads
items.text:
The chat needs a thread created first; open_thread runs once, before the first reply of each message, and adds its values:

"open_thread": {
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "https://chat.example.org/api/threads",
  "headers": [{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Bearer {{ .Secrets.token }}" }],
  "body": "{\"root\":\"{{ .Response.id }}\"}",
  "extract": [{ "name": "thread", "path": "$.thread.id" }]
},
"reply_in_thread": {
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "https://chat.example.org/api/threads/{{ .Response.thread }}/messages",
  "headers": [{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Bearer {{ .Secrets.token }}" }],
  "body": "{\"text\":{{ printf \"%s on #%d\" .Event .AlertGroup.Number | toJson }}}"
}

If open_thread fails, no reply is sent and the reply is retried by the usual rules; once it succeeded it does not run again for that message, whatever the reply after it came to.

items.title: Recipe: Storm summaries
items.text:
During a Storm, the Destination gets one Storm summary through create — Loud, first — and its later counts and final state through update, instead of the Alert Groups the Storm holds. Their templates see .Storm and no Alert Group, so templates that should handle both branch on it:

"body": "{\"text\":{{ if .Storm }}{{ printf \"Storm on %s: %d new Alert Groups, %d Urgent — %s\" .Storm.Route .Storm.AlertGroupCount .Storm.UrgentCount .Storm.URL | toJson }}{{ else }}{{ printf \"#%d %s (%s)\" .AlertGroup.Number .AlertGroup.Title .AlertGroup.Status | toJson }}{{ end }},\"over\":{{ if .Storm }}{{ .Storm.Final }}{{ else }}false{{ end }}}"

A template that reads .AlertGroup without the branch fails for a summary as a template error.

items.title: Mentions
items.text:
Muster does not know the chat's syntax for a Mention, so a Loud message carries its targets as data in .Mentions: each has Type (everyone, group or user) and, by type, Everyone (all, channel or here), Name, ID and Login. The trusted function mention renders a target as plain text — @all (or @channel, @here as the Mention settings chose), the group's name, or @ and the login — for the template to wrap in the chat's syntax:

{{ range .Mentions }}<{{ mention . }}> {{ end }}

items.title: Template errors
items.text:
A request whose template fails is not sent: that delivery or Thread reply ends as Not delivered with no fallback body, since the chat expects its own format. The Destination shows template_error with fallback not_sent, muster_template_errors_total{template="webhook_request"} grows, the log line webhook_template_failed names the request, and the Internal alert MusterTemplateError fires with the labels destination, destination_name and template. The next request of the Destination that renders clears the error and resolves the alert.

Preview a request template before you save it with POST /api/v1/template-previews and the kind webhook_request: it renders against a sample, with Secrets shown as [redacted] and extracted values as example-<name>.

items.title: Reference
items.text:
The pages of this section are generated from the code and the specification of this version of Muster.

  • Metrics: the metrics Muster serves at /metrics.
  • Log events: every line Muster logs.
  • Internal alerts: the problems Muster reports through its own pipeline, with their runbooks.
  • Environment variables: the bootstrap settings, read at start.
  • Chart values: the values of the Helm chart.
  • API: the conventions of the HTTP API and its reference, rendered from the specification.
  • Bridge protocol: the HTTP protocol between Muster and a bridge, and its reference, rendered from the specification.

items.title: API
items.text:
The API reference is rendered from api/openapi.yaml, the OpenAPI 3.1 document that the binary serves at /api/v1/openapi.yaml, so it describes this version of Muster. In short:

  • Listeners. The API is served under /api/v1 on the app listener, next to the UI; ingestion, Heartbeats and messenger callbacks under /api/v1 on the ingest listener; the health checks and /metrics on the internal listener.
  • Authentication. The UI uses a session cookie, with the X-CSRF-Token header on every request that changes something. Scripts send a Personal access token (mstr_pat_) or a Service account token (mstr_sat_) as a bearer token. An Integration token (mstr_int_) is accepted only by ingestion and the Heartbeat.
  • Identifiers. URLs carry the public_id of a resource: a type prefix of one or two letters and 12 characters of Crockford base32, such as AGK7M3QX9P2RTA; never the #N of an Alert Group.
  • Pagination. Lists take cursor and limit (50 by default, at most 500), and a page carries next_cursor.
  • Errors. Errors are RFC 9457 problems (application/problem+json) with a stable type, a stable code where a refusal needs one, and errors[] with a JSON pointer per invalid field. An operation that this version does not implement yet answers 501.
  • Concurrency. A configuration resource carries an ETag; an update sends it in If-Match and gets 412 when it no longer matches, 428 without it.
  • Values. Times are RFC 3339 in UTC; durations are whole seconds in *_seconds, retention periods whole days in *_days and measured latencies milliseconds in *_ms; enums are snake_case. Secrets are write-only: a read shows only whether one is set and when it was last changed, in <field>_status.
  • Rate limits. 429 with Retry-After, per token; ingestion is not rate-limited.

items.title: Bridge protocol
items.text:
The Bridge protocol is the HTTP protocol between Muster and a bridge, the separate service through which Muster delivers Alert Groups to a messenger it has no native support for: Muster calls the bridge to post, edit and reply, and the bridge reports presses, Thread messages, Account link requests and deleted messages back.

This is version 1.0.0 of the protocol. Every path is under /v1/, and a bridge reports protocol_version "1" in its answer to GET /v1/info. New optional fields and features keep version 1; a change that breaks existing bridges gets a new major path. The protocol is published under the MIT licence, so a bridge may stay closed.

  • The Bridge protocol reference is rendered from api/bridge.yaml, the OpenAPI document of the protocol, so it describes the protocol this version of Muster speaks.
  • The specification itself, as a raw file, is api/bridge.yaml on master.
  • Write a bridge is the guide: the bridge libraries first, then the protocol step by step.

items.text: The values of the Helm chart deploy/helm/muster. The types and the descriptions come from its values.schema.json, which rejects a value it does not list, and the defaults from its values.yaml. Set existingSecret: the chart never generates the master keys, and rendering fails without it.
