items.title: extraObjects
items.text:
array · default: []

Extra manifests that the chart renders into the release, each a document of its own, such as the ExternalSecret or the SealedSecret that produces existingSecret. An item is a map, or a string that holds a YAML manifest; both go through tpl, so a manifest can name .Values.existingSecret and .Release.Namespace. A {{ meant for another tool, such as the template of an ExternalSecret, is escaped as {{ `{{ .password | urlquery }}` }}; otherwise tpl renders it empty. Inside a map item, write the strings of an action with backticks: a map item is written back as YAML before tpl, which breaks lines longer than 80 characters at a space, and a double-quoted string cannot span that break.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text: Muster reads its bootstrap settings from these MUSTER_* environment variables at start, and no others; every other setting lives in the database and changes through the UI or the API. HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY are never read: each Connection, outgoing webhook Destination and the OIDC provider has its own proxy setting. A variable that is not set takes its default; one that has a default and is set but empty is an error. A secret can instead come from the file that its file form names, without one trailing line break; setting both forms is an error. An invalid value stops the start with an error that names the variable and never repeats the value of a secret, a variable marked so below.

items.title: MUSTER_DATABASE_URL
items.text:
no default · secret

The main database connection as a postgres:// or postgresql:// URL with the host, the user, the password and the database. Required unless MUSTER_DATABASE_HOST, MUSTER_DATABASE_NAME and MUSTER_DATABASE_USER are set; when both are given, the URL is used and the fields are ignored with a warning. Its pool_max_conns sets the size of a replica's main pool, max(10, CPUs) when it sets none. Its pool_* parameters apply to the main pool only; a session connection derived from it drops them.

items.title: MUSTER_DATABASE_HOST
items.text:
no default

The database host, when MUSTER_DATABASE_URL is not set.

items.title: MUSTER_DATABASE_PORT
items.text:
default: 5432

The database port, when MUSTER_DATABASE_URL is not set.

items.title: MUSTER_DATABASE_NAME
items.text:
no default

The database name; required unless MUSTER_DATABASE_URL is set.

items.title: MUSTER_DATABASE_USER
items.text:
no default

The database user; required unless MUSTER_DATABASE_URL is set.

items.title: MUSTER_DATABASE_PASSWORD
items.text:
no default · file form: MUSTER_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE · secret

The password of the database user, when MUSTER_DATABASE_URL is not set.

items.title: MUSTER_DATABASE_SSLMODE
items.text:
default: prefer

The sslmode of the database connections, when MUSTER_DATABASE_URL is not set: disable, allow, prefer, require, verify-ca or verify-full. muster doctor and the startup log report whether each connection is encrypted.

items.title: MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_URL
items.text:
no default · secret

The session connection, for advisory locks and LISTEN, as a postgres:// URL. Set it when the main connection goes through a pooler in transaction mode; unset, Muster uses the main connection without its pool_* parameters. A session connection has no pool, so pool_* parameters in this URL are ignored.

items.title: MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_HOST
items.text:
no default

The host of the session connection; its other fields are those of the main connection, without the pool_* parameters.

items.title: MUSTER_DATABASE_SESSION_PORT
items.text:
no default

The port of the session connection; its other fields are those of the main connection, without the pool_* parameters.

items.title: MUSTER_SECRET_KEYS
items.text:
no default · file form: MUSTER_SECRET_KEYS_FILE · secret

The master keys of the Keyring, which protect the secrets stored in the database: base64 keys of 32 bytes separated by commas, such as the output of openssl rand -base64 32; the file form holds one key per line. Required.

items.title: MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL
items.text:
no default

The address of Muster for people and messengers, an absolute http:// or https:// URL. Required. Browsers keep the session only over https:// or on localhost, so an http:// address on another host is logged as public_url_insecure at start.

items.title: MUSTER_INGEST_URL
items.text:
no default

The address Alertmanager sends its notifications to, an absolute http:// or https:// URL; unset, MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL.

items.title: MUSTER_LISTEN_APP
items.text:
default: :8080

The listen address of the app listener: the UI and the API.

items.title: MUSTER_LISTEN_INGEST
items.text:
default: :8081

The listen address of the ingest listener: ingestion, Heartbeats and messenger callbacks.

items.title: MUSTER_LISTEN_INTERNAL
items.text:
default: :8082

The listen address of the internal listener: the health checks and /metrics.

items.title: MUSTER_LOG_LEVEL
items.text:
default: info

The lowest level of the log lines written: info, warn or error.

items.title: MUSTER_MIGRATE_ON_START
items.text:
default: false

true applies the database migrations at start; the Helm chart migrates in an init container instead.

items.title: MUSTER_TRUSTED_PROXIES
items.text:
no default

The CIDR networks of the trusted reverse proxies, separated by commas. Empty, the client address of a request is its socket address; with networks listed, a request whose socket address is inside them takes the first address of X-Forwarded-For, read from the right, that is outside them.

items.title: MUSTER_RUNBOOK_BASE_URL
items.text:
default: https://muster-io.github.io/muster

The base of the runbook_url of Internal alerts: the published documentation site.

items.title: MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL
items.text:
no default

The email, also the login, of the bootstrap Admin, created at start when the Organization has no Admin; ignored once it has one.

items.title: MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD
items.text:
no default · file form: MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE · secret

The password of the bootstrap Admin; required with MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL while the Organization has no Admin.

items.title: Internal alerts
items.text: Muster reports problems it can still report through its own pipeline as Internal alerts: Alerts of the built-in "Muster" Integration, which every Organization has from the first start. Each raise and each resolve is a synthetic Stored Snapshot of that Integration, listed with its other Stored Snapshots and processed in order with them. Muster raises and resolves them explicitly when their condition changes; they are never resolved as Gone or Stale. Besides alertname and severity, a configuration entity appears by its immutable id (integration, route, destination) with its current name in a *_name label; the fingerprint is computed from alertname and the id label only, so renaming the entity updates the open Internal alert instead of raising a new one. Every Internal alert carries the annotations summary, description and runbook_url: MUSTER_RUNBOOK_BASE_URL, the major.minor of the binary (latest for any version that is not a release X.Y.Z) and the runbook below, joined by /. The capability is the one that raises it.

items.title: MusterDestinationBroken
items.text:
critical · labels: destination, destination_name · C-11 · runbook: operations/runbooks/MusterDestinationBroken/

Raised while: A Destination is Broken: the messenger answered with a Fatal error, or with Transient errors until the budget ran out, so its deliveries wait. It resolves when a probe, a Destination check or a Destination test succeeds.

items.title: MusterHeartbeatLost
items.text:
critical · labels: integration, integration_name, the Integration's Static labels · C-07 · runbook: operations/runbooks/MusterHeartbeatLost/

Raised while: An Integration is Heartbeat lost: no Heartbeat signal arrived within its Heartbeat timeout, so the path from its Alertmanager to Muster may be interrupted and Stale resolution is paused. It resolves with the next signal, when the Heartbeat is turned off or when the Integration is deleted.

items.title: MusterOIDCSecretExpiring
items.text:
warning · no labels · C-19 · runbook: operations/runbooks/MusterOIDCSecretExpiring/

Raised while: The OIDC client secret expires within oidc.secret_expiry_lead, by the expiry date an Admin entered in the OIDC settings. It resolves when the date moves further out or is removed.

items.title: MusterSnapshotTruncated
items.text:
warning · labels: integration, integration_name · C-06 · runbook: operations/runbooks/MusterSnapshotTruncated/

Raised while: An Integration has a truncated groupKey: Alertmanager cut a Snapshot with max_alerts, so Muster keeps the unlisted Alerts alive and cannot resolve them by absence. It resolves with the next untruncated Snapshot of every truncated groupKey.

items.title: MusterTemplateError
items.text:
warning · labels: route, route_name, destination, destination_name, template · C-12 · runbook: operations/runbooks/MusterTemplateError/

Raised while: A template of a Route failed while rendering a message, so its messages use the Fallback template; or a request template of an outgoing webhook Destination failed, so that request was not sent. It resolves when the template renders again or, for a Route, a new template is saved.

items.title: Log events
items.text: Muster writes one JSON object per line on stdout, and every line is one of the events below. A line has time (RFC 3339, UTC), level, event and the fields of its event; a secret is written as [redacted]. ERROR means someone must look within the hour, WARN that the line is needed for an investigation, INFO that an investigation is impossible without it; MUSTER_LOG_LEVEL sets the lowest level written. The capability is the one that logs the event.

items.title: account_link_linked
items.text:
INFO · fields: messenger, connection, user, error · C-18

A messenger account was linked to a User, through /start with a deep-link token in Telegram, a code from the bot's direct message in Mattermost or Slack, or through a Bridge an account_link event with a token sent to the bot or a code from the bot's direct message, and the account-links hint went to the User: messenger is telegram, mattermost, bridge or slack, connection the public_id of the Connection, user the public_id of the User. error, when present, says why the bot's confirmation or the answer to the account_link event was not sent; the link stays. Never carries the token or the code.

items.title: account_link_rejected
items.text:
INFO · fields: messenger, connection, reason, error · C-18

A link of a messenger account was refused and recorded as account_link.link_rejected: messenger is telegram, mattermost, bridge or slack, connection the public_id of the Connection, reason token_unknown, token_used, token_expired or wrong_connection for a /start or a Bridge account_link event, wrong_code, token_used or token_expired for a Mattermost, Bridge or Slack code, or conflict for an account linked to another User. error, when present, says why the bot's answer was not sent. Never carries the token or the code.

items.title: account_link_unlinked
items.text:
INFO · fields: messenger, connection, user, reason · C-18

An Account link was removed and recorded as account_link.unlink: messenger is telegram, mattermost, bridge or slack, connection the public_id of the Connection it was made through, user the public_id of its User, reason removed when the User or an Admin unlinked it, replaced when a new link of the User in the same identity space took its place, or user_deleted when its User was deleted.

items.title: active_key_not_held
items.text:
ERROR · fields: active_key_id, key_ids, error · C-02

The active master key is not in this replica's MUSTER_SECRET_KEYS, which happens when a key was activated while this replica's record had expired. The replica stops; add the key to its environment.

items.title: alert_continued
items.text:
INFO · fields: group, fingerprint · C-09

An Alert firing in an Alert Group got a new startsAt without being resolved in between (a Continuation, never a new firing): group is the #N of its Alert Group and fingerprint the Alert's.

items.title: alert_group_status_changed
items.text:
INFO · fields: group, route, from, to, reason, transport · C-09

An Alert Group changed status: group is its #N, route the public_id of its Route, from and to the statuses (from is empty for a new Alert Group), reason the reason of an automatic change and transport how the change reached Muster.

items.title: alert_groups_purged
items.text:
INFO · fields: details, summaries · C-09

The Alert Group retention of the Leader deleted, in batches, the Alerts inside Alert Groups that ended retention.alert_details ago (details, the rows deleted) and the summary rows of Alert Groups resolved retention.alert_group_summaries ago, with their Notes (summaries, the Alert Groups deleted).

items.title: alerts_stale
items.text:
INFO · fields: integration, count · C-06

The Stale scan resolved Alerts of an Integration with a live Heartbeat as Stale, because Alertmanager had not listed them for stale_after of live time in any Alertmanager group: integration is the public_id of the Integration and count how many Alerts resolved.

items.title: api_request_failed
items.text:
ERROR · fields: operation, error · C-03

An API request failed with an unexpected error, usually because the database was unavailable, and answered 500 internal; operation is the operationId of the specification.

items.title: audit_entry
items.text:
INFO · fields: entry, at, actor_kind, actor, actor_name, token_name, transport, action, resource_type, resource, resource_name, source_address, diff, details · C-03

An Audit log entry, as written to audit_log: the actor (its kind, the public_id of the user or Service account, or the --actor name of a CLI command), the token used, the Transport, the action ., the resource, the before/after diff of what was configured (a Secret shows only that it changed) and details.

items.title: bootstrap_admin_ignored
items.text:
WARN · fields: variables · C-03

The bootstrap Admin variables are set, but the Organization already has an Admin, so they were ignored and no user was created; remove them from the environment.

items.title: bootstrap_admin_missing
items.text:
WARN · no fields · C-03

The Organization has no Admin and the bootstrap variables are not set, so nobody can sign in to administer Muster: set MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL and MUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD (or _FILE) and restart, or run muster admin reset-password.

items.title: bridge_event_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: connection, event_id, type, error · C-22

The handling of a Bridge event failed — the read of a pushed event's Connection or of its secrets, its claim, the read of the message it names or of the Account link, or the deleted Root message flow — so its id was not recorded as handled: connection is the public_id of the Connection, event_id the event's id, type its type and error what failed; a failed read of the Connection comes before the event is authenticated, so its line has neither event_id nor type. In poll mode the cursor stays and the batch is polled again; in push mode the answer is 500 and the bridge sends the event again. Lines that keep coming for one event mean that the database refuses it.

items.title: bridge_event_rejected
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, reason · C-22

A Bridge event was refused and changed nothing: connection is the public_id the request named, empty when it is not a well-formed public_id, and reason why — unknown_connection (no Bridge Connection with this id, or a deleted one), poll_mode (the Connection receives its events by polling), signature (a webhook header is missing or no signature matches the push secret), timestamp (webhook-timestamp is further than bridge.push_tolerance from Muster's real clock), each answered 401; not_an_event (the body is no event of the Bridge protocol), id_mismatch (the event's id is not webhook-id) or too_large, each answered 400. A polled event that is no event is skipped with not_an_event, and the batch goes on. Never carries the signature, the push secret, the headers or the body.

items.title: bridge_info_read
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, protocol_version, features · C-22

Muster read the info of a Bridge Connection, on a Connection check or because its copy was older than bridge.info_max_age: connection is the public_id of the Connection, protocol_version the version the bridge speaks, features the names of the optional features it declares.

items.title: bridge_poll_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: connection, failures, error · C-22

A call of pollEvents of a Bridge Connection failed after the retries of the background client class, the cursor after a batch could not be stored, or the Connection's client could not be built: connection is the public_id of the Connection, failures how many calls in a row failed — for a client that cannot be built, how many reads of the Connections in a row found it so, counted for each version of the Connection, which is not polled meanwhile — and error what failed, masked of the token and the push secret. Logged at the first failure and every tenth; the poller backs off from 1 s to 1 min per call and polls again from the stored cursor. A failed poll makes no Destination Broken.

items.title: bridge_press
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, group, command, outcome, external_id, error · C-22

A press event of a Bridge Connection — a button press the bridge had already confirmed to its messenger — was handled, once its id was recorded: connection is the public_id of the Connection, external_id the messenger account that pressed; group the public_id of the Alert Group and command the Command, once the button data is verified against the pressed message; outcome done or unchanged for a Command that ran, which is not answered; refused, forbidden, not_linked, disabled or not_verified for a press that changed nothing; expired for a press on a Reminder whose button was signed by a key that is no longer in the Keyring; test for a press of a test message; unknown_message for a press on a message Muster did not post through the Connection, which is not answered; failed when the Command failed. Every outcome but done, unchanged and unknown_message is answered through answerEvent; error, when present, says why the press failed or why its answer was not made — no limiter token within the interactive budget, or the bridge refusing it — masked of the token. An answer that failed is not sent again.

items.title: bridge_press_dropped
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, external_id, age_seconds · C-22

A press event of a Bridge Connection arrived more than bridge.event_max_age after its occurred_at, by Muster's real clock, and was dropped without an answer: acting on it now could undo what people did since. connection is the public_id of the Connection, external_id the messenger account that pressed and age_seconds how old the press was. Nothing changed; the person can press again.

items.title: bridge_republished_past_edit_window
items.text:
INFO · fields: destination, group, old_message_id, new_message_id · C-22

The status of an Alert Group changed while its Bridge Root message was past the bridge's edit window, so Muster posted a new Root message Quietly and replied under the old one with a link to it: destination is the public_id of the Destination, group the public_id of the Alert Group, old_message_id and new_message_id the bridge's ids of the old and the new Root message. Later Thread replies go under the new one; the old one keeps working. Logged once the republication was recorded.

items.title: bridge_text_command
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, group, command, outcome, external_id, error · C-22

A thread_message event of a Bridge Connection was a Text command — one of the words of bridge.text_commands — and was handled once its id was recorded: connection is the public_id of the Connection, external_id the messenger account that wrote it, group the public_id of the Alert Group of the message whose Thread it is in, command the Command; outcome done or unchanged for a Command that ran, answered "Done: {command} #N"; refused, forbidden, not_linked, disabled or unknown_duration — a Snooze duration or preset the Route does not offer — for a Text command that changed nothing; unknown_message for one in the Thread of a message Muster did not post through the Connection, which is not answered; dropped for one older than bridge.event_max_age, which is not answered; failed when the Command failed. error, when present, says why the Command failed or why its answer was not made, masked of the token. Any other text in a Thread is neither answered nor logged.

items.title: clock_skew
items.text:
WARN · fields: skew_seconds, warning_seconds · C-02

This replica's clock differs from the database clock by more than process.clock_skew_warning; skew_seconds is positive when the replica's clock is ahead. Synchronise the clocks with NTP.

items.title: command_executed
items.text:
INFO · fields: command, group, actor, transport, outcome · C-10

A Command ran on an Alert Group: command is its name, group the public_id of the Alert Group, actor the public_id of the User or Service account, transport how it reached Muster and outcome done, or unchanged for an idempotent repeat such as Acknowledge by the current Owner.

items.title: command_refused
items.text:
INFO · fields: command, group, actor, transport, code · C-10

A Command was refused and changed nothing: command is its name, group the public_id of the Alert Group (empty for a bulk command refused as a whole), actor the public_id of the User or Service account, transport how it reached Muster and code forbidden for a missing Permission or the code of the command-refused problem.

items.title: database_connection_security
items.text:
INFO or WARN · fields: connection, sslmode, encrypted · C-02

Whether a database connection (main or session) is encrypted, with the sslmode in effect; WARN when it is not encrypted, which prefer allows without an error.

items.title: database_settings_conflict
items.text:
WARN · fields: used, ignored · C-02

A database connection is set both as a URL and as fields: the URL is used and the fields are ignored.

items.title: delivery_attempt
items.text:
INFO · fields: destination, group, kind, outcome, code, reason, attempt, duration_ms, retry_after_ms · C-11

The delivery worker called a Destination: destination is its public_id, group the #N of the Alert Group, empty for a Storm summary, kind what it sent (publication, update, thread_reply, storm_summary for any call of a Storm summary, final_edit for the last edit of a Root message in a Destination it left, or webhook_event for an event of an outgoing webhook in the events mode), outcome delivered or the error class of the answer, code the HTTP status of an answer that was not delivered, or the error_code a Telegram answer reports, 0 when it was delivered or the outcome carries no status, reason the masked error the messenger answered or the call failed with, empty when it was delivered, attempt the number of this attempt, duration_ms how long the call took and retry_after_ms the wait a RetryAfter asked for, 0 otherwise.

items.title: delivery_not_delivered
items.text:
WARN · fields: destination, group, kind, error_class · C-11

A delivery ended as Not delivered after an answer the adapter could not classify, because no adapter serves the Destination type, or because the Connection of its deleted Destination was deleted: destination is the public_id of the Destination, group the public_id of the Alert Group, empty for a Storm summary, kind what was sent (publication, update, thread_reply, storm_summary or final_edit) and error_class unknown. The next change of the Alert Group starts a new delivery.

items.title: delivery_possible_duplicate
items.text:
WARN · fields: destination, group · C-11

A Publication started again after an earlier start whose outcome was never recorded, such as after a crash, or, for a bridge, after a request that got no answer, and the bridge did not replay it: destination is the public_id of the Destination and group the public_id of the Alert Group. The messenger may show the Root message twice.

items.title: delivery_work_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: work, error · C-11

The delivery worker could not attempt a delivery or a Thread reply, or probe a Broken Destination (work is delivery, thread_reply or probe), or mark the first Publication of an Alert Group once its outcome committed (work is mark_published), because of error, such as a lost database connection. Any replica attempts it again once its lease runs out, or at the next probe; a first Publication is marked again by the next delivered call or event of the Alert Group.

items.title: destination_broken
items.text:
WARN · fields: destination, cause, reason · C-11

A Destination became Broken: destination is its public_id, cause fatal after a Fatal error or unavailable after the Transient budget ran out, and reason the masked error the messenger answered. Its deliveries wait, MusterDestinationBroken fires and a probe runs every delivery.broken_probe_interval.

items.title: destination_recovered
items.text:
INFO · fields: destination, broken_for_s · C-11

A Broken Destination is healthy again after a successful probe or Destination check: destination is its public_id and broken_for_s how long it was Broken, in seconds. Its deliveries resume with the current state.

items.title: destination_tested
items.text:
INFO · fields: destination, steps · C-16

A person tested a Destination: destination is its public_id and steps each step of the test with its error class, as name:class separated by commas, such as message:none,press:none; the class none is a step that succeeded, limited one that found no limiter token in time and sent nothing. The Audit log entry destination.tested records the same with the source.

items.title: dev_clock_load_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: error · C-01

Development mode only: the development clock could not be read after a change on another replica; this process keeps its offset until the next change or the next LISTEN.

items.title: dev_clock_loaded
items.text:
INFO · fields: offset_seconds · C-01

Development mode only: this process runs on the development clock, offset_seconds ahead of the system time, as stored in the database for every replica; logged at start and after each advance.

items.title: downtime_recorded
items.text:
WARN · fields: started_at, ended_at, duration_seconds · C-02

Muster was unavailable: no Leader wrote the alive mark and no replica refreshed its record for the period between started_at and ended_at. The new Leader recorded it and opened the recovery window (recovery.banner_duration).

items.title: fallback_template_used
items.text:
WARN · fields: route, group, template, error · C-12

A template of a Route failed while rendering a message, so the message used the Fallback template — every label under Muster's heading, footer and buttons: route is the public_id of the Route, group the public_id of the Alert Group, template the kind of template and error what failed, with its line and column. The Route shows a template error and MusterTemplateError fires until the template renders again. Logged once the change committed.

items.title: group_key_previewed
items.text:
INFO · fields: route, period_seconds, snapshots_read, truncated, duration_ms · C-08

A Group key preview read the Stored Snapshots of a period: route is the public_id of the saved Route it previewed, empty for a Route that is not saved yet, period_seconds the period, snapshots_read how many distinct bodies it read, truncated whether routing.group_key_preview_max_alerts stopped it with Stored Snapshots of the period, or Alerts the Route takes, left unread, and duration_ms how long it took.

items.title: heartbeat_live
items.text:
INFO · fields: integration, first · C-07

The Heartbeat of an Integration became live: integration is its public_id, and first is true for the first signal after the Heartbeat was turned on and false for a signal that ended a loss, which resolves MusterHeartbeatLost.

items.title: heartbeat_lost
items.text:
WARN · fields: integration, last_signal_at · C-07

No Heartbeat signal arrived for an Integration within its Heartbeat timeout, so it is Heartbeat lost and MusterHeartbeatLost is raised: integration is its public_id and last_signal_at the time of its last signal.

items.title: ingest_failed
items.text:
ERROR · fields: integration, route_pattern, error · C-05

An ingestion or Heartbeat request answered 500 because the database could not look up the token, store the Stored Snapshot or record the Heartbeat signal, usually because it was unavailable; Alertmanager retries an ingestion request, and the next signal replaces a lost one. integration is the public_id of the token's Integration, or unknown when the lookup failed; route_pattern is the route it came by.

items.title: ingest_rejected
items.text:
INFO · fields: integration, outcome, route_pattern, client_address · C-05

An ingestion or Heartbeat request was refused: outcome unauthorized (401, a missing, wrong or revoked token, an API token, or one of a deleted Integration) or too_large (413, a body above ingest.body_limit). integration is the public_id of the token's Integration, or unknown; route_pattern is the route it came by — never the path, which may carry the token — and client_address the sender. Refused ingestion requests are also counted in muster_ingest_requests_total, which the chart rule MusterIngestRejected reports.

items.title: ingest_replayed
items.text:
INFO · fields: actor, since, integration, count · C-06

muster ingest replay set the Stored Snapshots received within the period back to pending, for processing again: actor is the --actor name, since the period as given, integration the public_id of the Integration it was limited to, empty for all, and count how many Stored Snapshots it set back.

items.title: internal_alert_raised
items.text:
INFO · fields: alertname, fingerprint, entity · C-06

An Internal alert fired as an Alert of the built-in Muster Integration: alertname names it, fingerprint is the Alert's, and entity the public_id of the Integration, Route or Destination it is about, empty when it is about none.

items.title: internal_alert_resolved
items.text:
INFO · fields: alertname, fingerprint, entity · C-06

An Internal alert resolved because its condition cleared or its entity was deleted: alertname names it, fingerprint is the Alert's, and entity the public_id of the Integration, Route or Destination it is about, empty when it is about none.

items.title: key_activated
items.text:
WARN · fields: from, to, actor · C-20

muster secrets rotate-key activated a master key: every Secret and the key canary are now encrypted with it, the replicas switch to it and the Leader re-signs the buttons of the open Root messages. The old key stays in MUSTER_SECRET_KEYS until the Keyring shows it as removable.

items.title: key_canary_failed
items.text:
ERROR · fields: active_key_id, key_ids, error · C-02

The master keys cannot decrypt the key canary: the active key is missing from MUSTER_SECRET_KEYS, or the keys belong to another database. The replica stops; set the keys this database was written with.

items.title: key_switched
items.text:
INFO · fields: active · C-20

This replica switched to the active master key without a restart, after muster secrets rotate-key activated it: it now encrypts and signs with that key.

items.title: keyring_loaded
items.text:
INFO · fields: key_ids, active_key_id · C-02

The master keys of MUSTER_SECRET_KEYS were loaded and decrypt the key canary; the ids are derived from the keys and never reveal them.

items.title: leader_task_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: task, error · C-02

A run of a Leader task failed, usually because the database was unavailable; it runs again at its next interval.

items.title: leadership_acquired
items.text:
INFO · fields: replica · C-02

This replica took the Leader lock and runs the Leader tasks: partition maintenance, the alive mark, the pruning of replica records and the pruning of short-lived state.

items.title: leadership_lost
items.text:
WARN · fields: replica, error · C-02

The Leader could not confirm its lock within leader.fencing_timeout, or its lock session failed: it stopped every Leader task, closed the lock connection and competes for the lock again.

items.title: library_message
items.text:
WARN · fields: message · C-02

A third-party library wrote a line of its own, such as a failed read of the process metrics.

items.title: link_rule_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: link_rule, route, group, error · C-12

The URL template of a Link rule failed while computing the links of an Alert Group, so the rule's link is left out and muster_template_errors_total{template="link_rule"} grows: link_rule is the public_id of the Link rule, route the public_id of the Alert Group's Route, group the public_id of the Alert Group and error what failed, with its line and column. Logged once per rule and Alert Group on each replica; the counter grows at every failure.

items.title: listener_failed
items.text:
ERROR · fields: listener, error · C-02

A listener stopped serving with an error; the process stops so that it is restarted.

items.title: listeners_started
items.text:
INFO · fields: app, ingest, internal · C-02

The listeners serve and the process is ready; app and ingest are the same address when one port serves both.

items.title: live_updates_listen_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: error · C-03

A replica lost the session connection that listens for live-update hints, or could not open it, usually because the database was unavailable; it connects again with a growing delay, up to 30 seconds. Until then the browsers connected to it miss the hints of changes and see them at their next read.

items.title: live_updates_listen_restored
items.text:
INFO · no fields · C-03

A replica listens for live-update hints again after live_updates_listen_failed; it sent every connected browser the hints of everything, so that they read it again.

items.title: mattermost_press
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, group, command, outcome, answer, error · C-13

The callback of a Mattermost Connection received a button press and answered 200 with a JSON object, never with update: connection is the public_id of the Connection, empty when it does not exist; group the public_id of the Alert Group and command the Command, once the signed action id is verified; outcome done or unchanged for a Command that ran; refused, forbidden, not_linked, disabled or not_verified for a press that changed nothing and was answered, a not_verified one only on a post delivered to a Destination of the Connection in the channel of the press; expired for a press on a Reminder whose button was signed by a key that is no longer in the Keyring, answered that the button has expired; test for a press of a test message by a person, answered that nothing changed, and test_press for the bot's own press of it during a Destination test, answered with nothing; invalid_request for a body that is not a press, unknown_connection, or failed, answered once the press is bound to its post; answer how the person was answered: ephemeral_post for an ephemeral post in the channel, or in the Thread of the Root message for a press on a Reminder, ephemeral_text for the text in the callback's answer, shown in the Thread, when that post was not made, absent when nothing was answered; error why the press failed or why its ephemeral post was not sent, masked of secrets, never the 403 of a bot without the permission to make ephemeral posts.

items.title: migrations_applied
items.text:
INFO · fields: from, to · C-02

Migrations were applied under the migration lock, from one schema version to another.

items.title: migrations_current
items.text:
INFO · fields: version · C-02

No migration was applied: the schema already has the newest version this binary knows.

items.title: oidc_check_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: user, reason, error · C-03

A background re-check of an OIDC user at the identity provider found it unavailable — unreachable, a timeout, 408, 429 or 5xx, or the 10-second budget of the refresh spent — or could not run. Nothing changes for the user: sessions and Personal access tokens keep working, and the next attempt comes one auth.oidc_recheck_interval later, so an incident at the identity provider never signs everybody out. user is the public_id of the user, empty when a round of the worker failed; reason names the step; the error is masked and carries no token or secret.

items.title: oidc_secret_expiring
items.text:
WARN · fields: expires_on · C-19

The OIDC client secret expires within oidc.secret_expiry_lead, so MusterOIDCSecretExpiring is raised: expires_on is the expiry date entered in the OIDC settings. Logged once per raise.

items.title: oidc_sign_in_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: reason, error · C-03

An OIDC sign-in ended at the sign-in page, or the linking of an OIDC identity at the profile page, with idp_error: the identity provider reported an error, could not be reached through the back channel or its proxy, or answered with an ID token that did not verify. The reason names the step, prefixed with link for a link; the error is masked and carries no token or secret.

items.title: organization_created
items.text:
INFO · fields: organization · C-02

The first start created the Organization with the defaults of its settings and its outbound address policy.

items.title: organization_updated
items.text:
INFO · fields: fields · C-20

The Organization's settings changed; fields lists the JSON pointers of the changed fields, and the Audit log entry organization.updated has the values before and after (a Secret only as changed).

items.title: outbound_blocked
items.text:
WARN · fields: client, rule, scheme, host · C-02

The outbound address policy refused a request, which fails without retry; rule names the rule and the address or proxy it refused. Correct the configured address, or change the policy and its allowed networks.

items.title: outbound_policy_updated
items.text:
INFO · no fields · C-20

The outbound address policy changed: every replica drops its cached policy and closes its idle outbound connections at once, so the next request is checked against the new policy. The Audit log entry outbound_policy.updated has the values before and after.

items.title: outbound_unverified_address
items.text:
INFO · fields: client, scheme, host · C-02

A request went through the client's proxy to a host name that Muster cannot resolve itself, so only the name was checked against the allowed and denied lists, not its addresses.

items.title: outgoing_heartbeat_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: error · C-19

A send of the outgoing heartbeat to the dead man's switch failed and is not retried; the next interval sends again. error says what failed, without the URL. Logged at every failed send.

items.title: outgoing_heartbeat_recovered
items.text:
INFO · no fields · C-19

A send of the outgoing heartbeat succeeded after a failed one.

items.title: partition_maintenance_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: error · C-02

Partition maintenance failed, for example because a lock was not granted within 2 seconds; the Leader retries at the next hourly run. A partition that is still missing when its day or month begins makes writes to its table fail.

items.title: partitions_maintained
items.text:
INFO · fields: created, dropped · C-02

Partition maintenance created the partitions Muster will need (daily for Stored Snapshots and their bodies, monthly for Timeline entries, delivery events and the Audit log) or dropped partitions whose whole range is older than their retention period; the fields list the partitions by name.

items.title: process_started
items.text:
INFO · fields: version, commit · C-02

The server process started, with the version and commit of the binary.

items.title: process_stopped
items.text:
INFO · no fields · C-02

The server process stopped after a graceful shutdown.

items.title: public_url_insecure
items.text:
WARN · fields: host · C-03

MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL is a plain http:// address on a host other than localhost, a name under .localhost, 127.0.0.0/8 or ::1. The session cookie is Secure, so browsers drop it there and every sign-in returns to the sign-in page. Serve Muster over HTTPS through a reverse proxy or an Ingress, or open it through an SSH tunnel to localhost (ssh -L 8080:localhost:8080 to the host, then http://localhost:8080), and set MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL to that https:// or http://localhost:port address so that the warning stops. host is the host and port of MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL.

items.title: reminder_skipped
items.text:
INFO · fields: group, reason · C-17

A Reminder came due and was dropped with its timer: group is the public_id of the Alert Group and reason not_acknowledged when it is no longer acknowledged or policy_off when its Route's Reminders are off.

items.title: replica_record_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: replica, error · C-02

A replica could not refresh its record of the keys it holds, usually because the database is unavailable; it retries at the next refresh and stops counting as live once the record is older than replica.live_expiry. At shutdown, the record could not be deleted; it stops counting as live after replica.live_expiry.

items.title: replicas_pruned
items.text:
INFO · fields: replicas · C-02

The Leader removed the records of replicas that had not refreshed them for replica.prune_after.

items.title: request_log_pruned
items.text:
INFO · fields: rows · C-23

The Leader task request_log_pruning deleted, in batches, records of the Request log older than request_log.max_age or past the newest request_log.max_records of their Connection, of their outgoing webhook Destination or of the records without an owner: rows is how many it deleted in one run. Not logged when a run deleted nothing.

items.title: request_log_write_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: direction, operation, owner, error · C-23

A record of the Request log could not be written — the database refused it, or its write ran past its 2 s timeout — and was dropped; the request it records went on unchanged. direction and operation are the record's, owner the public_id of its Connection or outgoing webhook Destination, empty without one, and error the database error. The headers and bodies of the record are never logged; muster_request_log_write_failures_total counts the dropped records.

items.title: schema_dirty
items.text:
ERROR · fields: database_version · C-02

A migration failed halfway and the schema is marked dirty at its version: repair the schema from a backup or by hand, then clear the dirty flag in schema_migrations.

items.title: schema_too_new
items.text:
ERROR · fields: database_version, known_version · C-02

The database schema is newer than this binary knows, after an upgrade was rolled back: run a release that knows the schema version.

items.title: schema_too_old
items.text:
ERROR · fields: database_version, known_version · C-02

The database schema is older than this binary needs: run muster migrate or set MUSTER_MIGRATE_ON_START.

items.title: short_lived_pruned
items.text:
INFO · fields: table, rows · C-02

The hourly short-lived pruning of the Leader deleted, in batches, rows of a short-lived table that can no longer be used, such as sessions that ended or expired auth.session_prune_after ago, sign-in throttles without a failure for auth.signin_throttle_prune_after, password setup links that expired auth.password_setup_prune_after ago and Account link requests that expired account_link.request_prune_after ago; rows is how many it deleted from the table.

items.title: shutdown_grace_exceeded
items.text:
WARN · fields: grace_seconds · C-02

Requests were still running when the shutdown grace period ended; their connections were closed.

items.title: shutdown_requested
items.text:
WARN · fields: grace_seconds · C-02

The server received SIGTERM or an interrupt: readiness answers 503, work in progress finishes and the listeners drain within the grace period, in seconds.

items.title: slack_press
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, group, command, outcome, answer, error · C-24

A press of a Slack Connection was handled after Slack had its confirmation — the 200 of the callback in http mode: connection is the public_id of the Connection; group the public_id of the Alert Group and command the Command, once the signed action id is verified against the pressed message, the command alone for a test message; outcome done or unchanged for a Command that ran, which is not answered but "Still on it", which changes no message; refused, forbidden, not_linked, disabled or not_verified for a press that changed nothing and was answered; expired for a press on a Reminder whose button was signed by a key that is no longer in the Keyring, answered that the button has expired; test for a press of a test message, answered that nothing changed; ignored for another kind of interaction, confirmed and not answered; failed when a read or the Command failed, or when the Connection could not be read and the callback answered 500. answer is how the person was answered: ephemeral for chat.postEphemeral in the channel of the press, in the Thread of the Root message for a press on a Reminder, or response_url for the press's response_url when that failed; absent when nothing was answered. error says why the press failed or why its answer was not made, with the tokens, the Slack signing secret and the response_url masked; an answer that fails both ways is not made again.

items.title: slack_press_rejected
items.text:
WARN · fields: connection, reason · C-24

A request to the callback of Slack presses in http mode was refused and changed nothing: connection is the public_id of the Connection when it is known; reason why — bad_signature (X-Slack-Signature is missing or is not the signature of the body under the Connection's Slack signing secret), stale (X-Slack-Request-Timestamp is missing or further than slack.request_tolerance from Muster's real clock, either way), unknown_connection (no Slack Connection with this id, or a deleted one) or wrong_mode (the Connection receives its presses through Socket Mode), each answered 401 with the same body; no_payload (the body has no payload that is a JSON object) or too_large (the body is over 1 MiB), each answered 400. Lines that keep coming with bad_signature mean a wrong Slack signing secret or someone else's requests. Never carries the signature, the Slack signing secret, the headers or the body.

items.title: slack_socket_connected
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, num_connections, held, error · C-24

The Leader's Socket Mode connection of a Slack Connection received its hello: connection is the public_id of the Connection, num_connections the connections of the Slack app that Slack counts, this one included, and held how many of them the Leader holds for the Connection — two while a planned refresh overlaps the next connection with the old one. The count beyond held is stored on the Connection for its check and page, and the line is written once it was; error, when present, says that it could not be stored within 5 s, and the next hello stores it again. A hello whose count the next hello replaces before it is stored has no line: only the next one is stored and logged; nor has a store that the Leader's stop cut short.

items.title: slack_socket_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: connection, reason, backoff_seconds, error · C-24

A Socket Mode connection of a Slack Connection could not be opened or ended without a planned refresh: connection is the public_id of the Connection; reason dial (apps.connections.open failed, the address it answered is not Slack's, the WebSocket handshake failed or the Connection's client could not be built), hello_timeout (no hello within slack.hello_timeout), link_disabled (Socket Mode was turned off in the app's settings), too_many_websockets (the app already has ten connections) or closed (the connection ended, a ping got no pong within 10 s or a confirmation could not be written); backoff_seconds the wait before the next connection, from 1 s doubling with jitter up to 5 min (slack.socket_backoff), never shorter than the Retry-After of a rate-limited apps.connections.open, up to that cap, and reset by a hello once its connection has lasted 30 s, or by a planned refresh — absent when the Connection's client could not be built; error what failed, with the tokens and the address's query, the ticket among it, masked, absent for hello_timeout, link_disabled and too_many_websockets. It counts against nothing and makes no Destination Broken; presses made until the next hello are lost.

items.title: slack_socket_shared
items.text:
WARN · fields: connection, other_connections · C-24

A hello of a Slack Connection's Socket Mode connection counted more connections of the Slack app than the Leader holds: another program — usually another Connection or Muster installation on the same app — is connected and takes some of its presses at random. connection is the public_id of the Connection and other_connections the connections beyond the Leader's. Right after a Leader change Slack may still count the old Leader's connection; a later hello clears the count. Use one Slack app for each Connection and share it with no other Connection or installation.

items.title: snapshot_accepted
items.text:
INFO · fields: integration, stored_snapshot, size_bytes, route_pattern · C-05

An ingestion request was stored as a pending Stored Snapshot and answered 202: integration and stored_snapshot are public_ids, size_bytes the size of the body, route_pattern the route it came by — never the path, which may carry the token.

items.title: snapshot_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: integration, stored_snapshot, error · C-06

A Stored Snapshot could not be processed and was marked failed with the error: its body is not JSON, lacks the fields of an Alertmanager webhook, or processing failed. It is not retried by itself, the Snapshots behind it are processed, and muster ingest replay processes it again after a fix. integration and stored_snapshot are public_ids.

items.title: snapshot_processed
items.text:
INFO · fields: integration, stored_snapshot, group_key, alerts, fired, resolved, gone, continued, dropped, truncated, routes, alert_groups, duration_ms, lane · C-06

A Stored Snapshot was processed: integration and stored_snapshot are public_ids, group_key the Alertmanager group it came for, alerts how many Alerts it listed, fired, resolved, gone and continued how many new firings, resolutions from Alertmanager or by the deletion of the Integration, Alerts resolved as Gone and Continuations it made, dropped the resolves of fingerprints that fire nowhere, truncated its truncatedAlerts, routes the public_ids of the Routes that took its newly firing Alerts, alert_groups the #N of the Alert Groups it created or changed, duration_ms how long processing took, and lane which of the Integration's processing.parallel_groups lanes processed it, from 0.

items.title: snapshot_processing_interrupted
items.text:
WARN · fields: integration, error · C-06

The processing worker stopped a round or an Integration because the database failed or the connection was lost; the Stored Snapshots stay pending and are processed at the next attempt, after a growing pause. integration is the public_id of the Integration, empty when the round failed.

items.title: startup_failed
items.text:
ERROR · fields: error · C-02

Startup stopped: the database cannot be reached or fails a check, a migration failed, or a listener cannot listen. The error says what to fix.

items.title: storm_ended
items.text:
INFO · fields: route, alert_groups, urgent · C-11

A Storm ended after its Route stayed at or below route.storm_threshold for delivery.storm_calm_period: route is the public_id of the Route, and alert_groups and urgent are the Storm's own counts at its end, as storm_started has them at its start: the new Alert Groups it counted and how many of them were Urgent. The Storm summary shows its final state and the Alert Groups still open are posted Quietly.

items.title: storm_started
items.text:
INFO · fields: route, alert_groups, urgent · C-11

The new Alert Groups of a Route exceeded route.storm_threshold within a minute and started a Storm: route is the public_id of the Route, and alert_groups and urgent are the Storm's own counts at its start, as storm_ended has them at its end: the new Alert Groups it counted, 1 (the one that started it), and how many of them were Urgent, 1 or 0. Each Destination of the Route gets a Storm summary and only Urgent Alert Groups are posted one by one until it calms down. Logged once the change that started it committed.

items.title: system_notices_check_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: error · C-03

A replica could not read the state of the Organization-wide notices, usually because the database was unavailable, so the live-updates streams get no hint of a notice that started or ended; logged once until a check succeeds again.

items.title: telegram_poll_conflict
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, backoff_ms · C-14

The long poll of a Telegram Connection was refused with 409 Conflict: another process polls the same bot, or a webhook is set for it. The poller waits backoff_ms, with jitter, and polls again; it is not a delivery outcome and makes nothing Broken. connection is the public_id of the Connection. Lines that keep coming mean that a second installation polls the bot, or that its webhook was set elsewhere: the connection check shows it.

items.title: telegram_poll_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: connection, error · C-14

A long poll of a Telegram Connection failed after the retries of the background client class, or an update it brought could not be handed to the router: connection is the public_id of the Connection, error what failed, with the bot token and the path prefix of the base URL masked. The poller backs off and polls again from the stored offset.

items.title: telegram_press
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, group, command, outcome, error · C-14

A callback_query of a Telegram Connection — a button press — was handled and answered with answerCallbackQuery before the Root message was edited: connection is the public_id of the Connection; group the public_id of the Alert Group and command the Command, once the button data is verified; outcome done or unchanged for a Command that ran; refused, forbidden, not_linked, disabled or not_verified for a press that changed nothing; expired for a press on a Reminder whose button was signed by a key that is no longer in the Keyring, answered that the button has expired; test for a press of a test message, answered that nothing changed; failed when a read or the Command failed. error, when present, says why the press failed or why its answer was not made — no limiter token within the interactive budget, or Telegram refusing an answer that came too late — masked of the bot token. The update is confirmed whatever the outcome, so that a press never runs twice.

items.title: telegram_press_dropped
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, gap_seconds · C-14

A button press of a Telegram Connection arrived after the Connection had received no updates for longer than telegram.press_max_age — no successful long poll, or Muster not running — and was dropped without an answer: Telegram kept it during the gap, and acting on it now could undo what people did since. connection is the public_id of the Connection, gap_seconds the gap before the update that carried the press. Nothing changed; the person can press again.

items.title: telegram_update_dropped
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, kind · C-14

An update of a Telegram Connection reached the update router, which has no handler for its kind and drops it: connection is the public_id of the Connection, kind one of callback_query, chat_message, private_message, my_chat_member or other. Private messages, such as /start, go to the handler of Account links.

items.title: telegram_update_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: connection, error · C-14

The webhook endpoint of a Telegram Connection could not look up the Connection or hand the update to the router, usually because the database was unavailable, and answered 500; Telegram sends the update again. connection is the public_id from the path, error what failed.

items.title: telegram_webhook_delete_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: connection, error · C-14

A Telegram Connection in the webhook update mode was deleted, and deleteWebhook, called with its bot and base URL as a best effort after the deletion, failed: connection is the public_id of the Connection, error what Telegram or the network answered, without the bot token. The deletion stands; Telegram keeps posting the bot's updates to Muster, which answers them 401, until the webhook is removed with the bot's token elsewhere.

items.title: telegram_webhook_deleted
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection · C-14

A Telegram Connection in the webhook update mode was deleted and deleteWebhook, called with its bot and base URL after the deletion, removed its webhook: connection is the public_id of the Connection.

items.title: telegram_webhook_set
items.text:
INFO · fields: connection, host · C-14

A Telegram Connection was saved in the webhook update mode and setWebhook set its webhook, with a new secret token, at MUSTER_INGEST_URL: connection is the public_id of the Connection, host the host of the webhook's URL.

items.title: template_recovered
items.text:
INFO · fields: route, template · C-12

A template of a Route that kept failing rendered again: route is the public_id of the Route and template the kind of template. The Route's template error is cleared and MusterTemplateError resolves. Logged once the change committed.

items.title: timer_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: kind, error · C-09

A timer could not fire: kind is the timer kind and error what failed. The timer fires again on any replica once its lease runs out.

items.title: timer_fired
items.text:
INFO · fields: kind, group, notice, missed · C-17

A timer of an Alert Group fired: kind is ack_timeout or reminder, group the public_id of the Alert Group, notice the number of the notice or Reminder it sent, or of the last one a collapse stands for, and missed how many overdue ones collapsed into one notices_missed, 0 when none did.

items.title: webhook_event_not_delivered
items.text:
WARN · fields: destination, group, lifecycle_event, status · C-15

An event of an outgoing webhook in the events mode ended as Not delivered after an answer that is not retried and does not make the Destination Broken — 400, 413, 422, a redirect, which is never followed, or another unknown answer — or because its request template failed: destination is the public_id of the Destination, group the public_id of the Alert Group, lifecycle_event the lifecycle event and status the HTTP status of the answer, empty without one. The next event of the Alert Group follows.

items.title: webhook_template_failed
items.text:
WARN · fields: destination, group, request, error · C-15

A request template of an outgoing webhook failed, so that request was not sent and its delivery, Thread reply or event ended as Not delivered with no fallback body: destination is the public_id of the Destination, group the public_id of the Alert Group, empty for a Storm summary, request the request — create, update, open_thread, reply_in_thread or events — and error what failed, with its line and column and every Secret masked. The Destination shows a template error and MusterTemplateError fires until one of its requests renders again. Logged once the outcome is recorded.

items.title: webhook_value_missing
items.text:
WARN · fields: destination, group, rule · C-15

An extraction rule of the "create" or "open thread" request of an outgoing webhook found nothing in the response: destination is the public_id of the Destination, group the public_id of the Alert Group and rule the name of the rule. The request counts as delivered and the Timeline records template_value_missing; a later request that reads the value fails as a template error. Logged once the outcome is recorded.

items.title: Metrics
items.text: Muster serves these metrics in the Prometheus text format at /metrics on the internal listener and never pushes them; the endpoint also serves the process (process_*) and Go runtime (go_*) metrics. Configuration entities appear only by their public_id (integration, route, destination); the labels of an *_info metric carry what it describes, such as a name or the version; every other label takes its values from the closed set listed below. Histograms are Prometheus histograms with le buckets. A Leader-only metric is exported only by the replica that is the Leader. The capability is the one that exports the metric.

items.title: muster_alert_group_time_to_ack_seconds
items.text:
histogram · labels: route · C-10 · exported by every replica

Time from the start of an Alert Group to its first acknowledgement, observed once per Alert Group, by Route.

Buckets (le): 60, 300, 600, 1800, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 43200, 86400.

  • route (entity): the public_id of the route

items.title: muster_alert_group_time_to_resolve_seconds
items.text:
histogram · labels: route · C-09 · exported by every replica

Time from the start of an Alert Group to its resolution, observed at each resolution, by Route.

Buckets (le): 60, 300, 600, 1800, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 43200, 86400.

  • route (entity): the public_id of the route

items.title: muster_alert_groups
items.text:
gauge · labels: route, status · C-09 · exported by the Leader only

Open Alert Groups by Route and status, counted by the Leader; an Alert Group moved to the Default route counts there.

  • route (entity): the public_id of the route
  • status: firing, acknowledged, snoozed — the status of the open Alert Groups

items.title: muster_alert_groups_created_total
items.text:
counter · labels: route · C-09 · exported by every replica

Alert Groups that started, by Route.

  • route (entity): the public_id of the route

items.title: muster_alert_groups_reopened_total
items.text:
counter · labels: route · C-09 · exported by every replica

Alert Groups that reopened within their Route's Reopen window, by Route.

  • route (entity): the public_id of the route

items.title: muster_alert_groups_resolved_total
items.text:
counter · labels: route, by · C-09 · exported by every replica

Alert Groups that were resolved, by Route and by who resolved them.

  • route (entity): the public_id of the route
  • by: user, system — user is a person's resolve, system the resolve when the last Alert resolved

items.title: muster_alerts_resolved_total
items.text:
counter · labels: integration, reason · C-06 · exported by every replica

Alerts that resolved, by Integration and reason.

  • integration (entity): the public_id of the integration
  • reason: resolved, gone, stale, integration_deleted — resolved is a resolve from Alertmanager, for the Alert or its whole Alertmanager group; gone an Alert Alertmanager no longer lists; stale one not seen for stale_after with a live Heartbeat; integration_deleted one of a deleted Integration

items.title: muster_build_info
items.text:
gauge · labels: version, commit · C-02 · exported by every replica

Always 1; the labels carry the version and commit of the running binary.

  • version (info): the release version of the binary, such as 1.4.0
  • commit (info): the Git commit the binary was built from

items.title: muster_client_request_duration_seconds
items.text:
histogram · labels: client, outcome · C-02 · exported by every replica

Duration of outbound HTTP requests, one per attempt, from the dial to the end of the body, by client class and outcome.

Buckets (le): 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 30, 60.

  • client: delivery, interactive, background, heartbeat — the client class of ADR-0015
  • outcome: ok, retry_after, transient, fatal, unknown, blocked, redirect — the classified outcome of the request

items.title: muster_client_requests_total
items.text:
counter · labels: client, outcome · C-02 · exported by every replica

Outbound HTTP requests, one per attempt, by client class and classified outcome.

  • client: delivery, interactive, background, heartbeat — the client class of ADR-0015
  • outcome: ok, retry_after, transient, fatal, unknown, blocked, redirect — the classified outcome of the request

items.title: muster_clock_skew_seconds
items.text:
gauge · no labels · C-02 · exported by every replica

This replica's clock minus the database clock, corrected by half the round trip; positive when the replica is ahead.

items.title: muster_commands_total
items.text:
counter · labels: command, transport, outcome · C-10 · exported by every replica

Commands run on Alert Groups, one per Alert Group, by command, Transport and outcome.

  • command: acknowledge, unacknowledge, resolve, unresolve, snooze, unsnooze, add_note, still_on_it — the Command
  • transport: ui, api, mattermost, telegram, bridge, slack, system — how the Command reached Muster
  • outcome: done, unchanged, refused, skipped, failed — done changed the Alert Group, unchanged was an idempotent repeat, refused a refusal or a missing Permission, skipped an Alert Group a bulk Acknowledge left to its Owner, failed an Alert Group that was not found

items.title: muster_db_pool_acquire_wait_seconds_total
items.text:
counter · no labels · C-02 · exported by every replica

Seconds spent waiting for a connection of the main database pool of this replica, summed over every acquire.

items.title: muster_db_pool_acquires_total
items.text:
counter · no labels · C-02 · exported by every replica

Connections taken from the main database pool of this replica.

items.title: muster_db_pool_connections
items.text:
gauge · labels: state · C-02 · exported by every replica

Connections of the main database pool of this replica, by state.

  • state: acquired, idle, constructing — the state of the connection

items.title: muster_db_pool_max_connections
items.text:
gauge · no labels · C-02 · exported by every replica

The most connections the main database pool of this replica opens.

items.title: muster_delivery_attempts_total
items.text:
counter · labels: destination, kind, outcome · C-11 · exported by every replica

Calls of the delivery worker to a Destination, one per attempt, by Destination, what it sent and its outcome.

  • destination (entity): the public_id of the destination
  • kind: publication, update, thread_reply, storm_summary, final_edit, webhook_event — publication is a new Root message, update an edit of one, thread_reply a reply in its Thread, storm_summary and final_edit those messages, webhook_event an event of an outgoing webhook
  • outcome: delivered, markup_rejected, retry_after, transient, fatal, unknown, template_error — delivered, or the error class of the answer

items.title: muster_delivery_latency_seconds
items.text:
histogram · labels: destination · C-11 · exported by every replica

Time from the receipt of the Snapshot behind a change of a Root message, or behind an event of an outgoing webhook, to the API call that delivered it, by Destination; changes made by Commands or timers are not observed. The service-level indicator of NFR-2.

Buckets (le): 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 30, 60, 300, 900.

  • destination (entity): the public_id of the destination

items.title: muster_delivery_queue
items.text:
gauge · labels: destination · C-11 · exported by the Leader only

Pending deliveries and Thread replies that are due, per Destination that is not deleted, counted by the Leader.

  • destination (entity): the public_id of the destination

items.title: muster_destination_broken
items.text:
gauge · labels: destination · C-11 · exported by the Leader only

1 while the Destination is Broken, 0 while it is healthy, per Destination that is not deleted; set by the Leader.
